claims.hypothesis: The compact sources are Stage 0/I YSOs rather than HII regions, prestellar cores or Stage II/III
claims.experiment: Brightness temperature and spectral-index modelling, Stromgren sphere, free-fall time, Bonnor-Ebert mass and disk-mass extrapolation
claims.result: Sources consistent with ~50 K, partially optically thick disks; few HII contaminants
claims.finding: Sample is primarily Stage 0/I YSOs, warmer than local disks

evidence.quote: We therefore conclude that the sample is comprised primarily of Stage 0/I YSOs.

claims.hypothesis: The core mass function is top-heavy in Sgr B2
claims.experiment: Power-law fit with plfit to 3 mm lower-limit masses above 6 sigma completeness
claims.finding: The core mass function is consistent with the Kroupa IMF

evidence.quote: We find that the core mass function of our sample is consistent with the Kroupa IMF.

claims.hypothesis: Source counting gives the stellar mass and star formation rate of Sgr B2 N and M
claims.experiment: Core-based plus HII-region-based mass with Kroupa IMF extrapolation and 0.74 Myr age
claims.finding: Total SFR 0.013 Msun/yr, similar to previous estimates

evidence.quote: Using direct source counting, we infer the total stellar mass of 2800M$_\odot$ for Sgr B2 N and 6900M$_\odot$ for Sgr B2 M.

why_this_data.value: Follow-up at higher resolution to the earlier ALMA Band 3 survey of the region

evidence.quote: We report follow-up ALMA observations to ALMA project 2013.1.00269.S

why_this_method.value: Fully automated source detection is inefficient in this high dynamic range, complex field, so dendrograms plus manual vetting were used

evidence.quote: Combining this with the irregular structure of the observed objects makes fully automated source detection inefficient.
Therefore, we utilized the automated source-finding dendrogram algorithm (cite: Rosolowsky2008) augmented with a by-hand approach described below.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: 2D Gaussian photometry rejected in favor of dendrogram contours

evidence.quote: Thus, we concluded that our sources are not well-represented by simple 2D Gaussians and decided to use dendrogram contours to define sources.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Mosaic gridder for the overlapping Band 3 pointings rejected

evidence.quote: We find no significant benefit of imaging the two pointings together with mosaic gridder when compared to using standard gridder on each pointing individually.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: RMS-based clean masks replaced by hand-drawn polygons

evidence.quote: At first, we tried to use RMS-based masks.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: More conservative self-calibration tested but gives 20% higher noise

evidence.quote: With the self-calibration approach used in this paper, we are able to achieve 20% lower noise compared to the more conservative self-calibration.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Self-calibration stopped at the step where noise stopped improving; extra step added only for Sgr B2 N Band 6

evidence.quote: Running this extra self-calibration step on the other pointings did not reduce the noise in the images.

limitations_admitted.value: Hand-drawn exclusion polygons can remove true sources

evidence.quote: Excluding detections within polygons that were drawn by eye can potentially exclude true positives.

limitations_admitted.value: Local imaging artifacts (negative bowls, wave patterns) remain after self-calibration

evidence.quote: Even after extensive self-calibration and cleaning, the data still include local artifacts such as negative bowls around bright sources and wave-like patterns on different scales.

limitations_admitted.value: Masses are lower limits and may be underestimated, especially in crowded regions

evidence.quote: Thus, even with this correction some masses might be underestimated.
We note that the difference between a score of 1 and 2 is subjective.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single assumed T = 50 K and optically thin kappa for all cores; masses are lower limits by construction and the mass function slope depends on this.
Only 60% of 3 mm sources lie in the 1 mm field, so spectral-index conclusions are extrapolated.
Hand scoring of cores and hand-drawn masks make the catalog hard to reproduce exactly.
Flux scatter up to 40% per source from self-calibration choices; no ALMA absolute flux uncertainty quoted.
Mass function compared with Kroupa IMF without a completeness-corrected treatment of fragmentation or unresolved multiplicity.

code_released.value: Image reduction code and final catalogs on GitHub (nbudaiev/SgrB2_ALMA_continuum), including polygon regions

evidence.quote: Image reduction and final catalogs are available on GitHub: <https://github.com/nbudaiev/SgrB2_ALMA_continuum/releases/tag/Accepted-15-Sep-2023>.
The polygon regions are available on GitHub with the rest of the reduction code: <https://github.com/nbudaiev/SgrB2_ALMA_continuum>
The FITS files of the self-calibrated data were published in a Zenodo repository at [doi:10.5281/zenodo.8377186](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8377186).

missing_for_reproduction: tclean cell/image size, niter, deconvolver, and per-pointing absolute clean thresholds
Self-calibration solution parameters of the original reduction (refant, minsnr, combine)
Subjective per-source scores (obtainable from the released catalog)
Pipeline version / calibrators used to produce the delivered calibrated data
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Several hundred GB: four execution blocks, 43-46 12 m antennas, 4 x 1920 channels per band, baselines to 12 km, ~2600-3000 s each (calibrated MS plus cleaning products)
reproducibility.score_reason: Public ALMA projects, released code, catalogs and images, and numeric results, but several imaging/self-cal parameters are unstated and core vetting is manual and subjective.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: ALMA projects are named and code, polygons and catalogs are released; main results are numeric counts, masses, slopes and SFRs, though the manual vetting limits exact recovery.
